summary.title: Day 5: Creating INI Parser
summary.one_liner: Learn how to write a small, pure-Nim INI file parser built on tables, with a simple line-based state machine and helper procs for reading and editing sections and properties.
takeaways: An INI file is made of sections in [brackets], each holding key = value pairs.
Nim's Table type can model sections and their properties, with ref objects wrapping them.
A two-state line parser (readSection, readKV) skips blank lines and ; or # comments, then splits on '='.
Helper procs like getProperty, setProperty, hasSection and toIniString make the parsed document editable and serializable.
summary.summary: The post builds a pure Nim INI parser without regular expressions or PCRE, explaining that Nim's built-in parsecfg already exists. It defines Section and Ini types backed by tables, with an API for getting, setting, checking and deleting sections and properties, plus toIniString for output. The parser splits input into lines, ignores blanks and comments, and uses a readSection/readKV state machine to assign key-value pairs to the current section.
